methodology:
AAC owns approximately 6.5 million hectares (~16.1 million acres) of pastoral cattle stations across Queensland and the Northern Territory — roughly 1% of Australia's total land mass. The portfolio is heavily concentrated: top 7 named stations alone total ~12.6M acres, with Brunette Downs alone at 3M acres.

Pastoral cattle station valuations operate at very different per-acre levels from cropland. 2024-2025 Australian pastoral transactions price between $200-400 AUD/acre depending on:
- Carrying capacity (head per hectare, varies with rainfall and pasture quality)
- Water reliability (Barkly Tableland has good bore water; VRD has better stream access)
- Cattle market cycle position
- State (QLD generally trades at slight premium to NT)

AAC's GAAP balance sheet (Net PP&E AUD 1,723M) carries land at long-held cost basis — much of the portfolio was acquired decades ago at minimal per-acre cost. Compared against current pastoral comps of $230-380 AUD/acre, the implied current FMV is meaningfully higher than book.

Per-property book values shown are estimates allocated by area share of total Net PP&E — AAC doesn't publish per-station book in its annual report. The aggregate FMV reflects current pastoral comps applied across the portfolio.

Note that AAC's earnings volatility (FY25 statutory EBITDA -$221M due to biological asset revaluation losses) does not reflect land FMV — pastoral land values are stable relative to cattle market cycles. This is the analytical case for AAC: long-duration land asset with inherent cattle market exposure that's more volatile than the underlying real estate.
